items.name: F-1
items.description: The most powerful single-chamber liquid rocket engine flown. Burned kerosene and liquid oxygen on the Saturn V first stage.
items.source: NASA S-IC fact sheet / public Rocketdyne F-1 documentation (values approximate)

items.name: J-2
items.description: Hydrogen-fueled upper-stage engine used on the Saturn V second and third stages. Restartable in flight, which made the trans-lunar injection burn possible.
items.source: NASA Saturn V news reference (SL thrust theoretical, ignited in vacuum)

items.name: Merlin 1D
items.description: Modern high-thrust kerosene engine. Nine of them power the Falcon 9 first stage.

items.name: Merlin Vacuum
items.description: Vacuum-optimized Merlin with a large expansion nozzle. Powers the Falcon 9 second stage and can restart in orbit.
items.source: SpaceX Merlin Vacuum public specifications (values approximate)

items.name: RD-180
items.description: Twin-chamber kerosene engine that powers the Atlas V first stage. Extremely efficient for its class.
items.source: NPO Energomash / ULA public specifications (values approximate)

items.name: RS-25
items.description: Reusable hydrogen engine from the Space Shuttle, now used as the SLS core stage engine. The most efficient engine in the catalog.

items.name: RL10C-1
items.description: Compact, highly efficient hydrogen upper-stage engine used on Centaur and the SLS interim cryogenic propulsion stage.
items.source: Aerojet Rocketdyne RL10 public specifications (values approximate)

items.name: AJ10 (spacecraft engine)
items.description: Reliable storable-propellant spacecraft engine (Apollo service module heritage). Included with crewed spacecraft for orbit and return burns.
items.source: NASA Apollo SPS / AJ10 heritage documentation (values approximate)
